clue.text: Debatable issue theologian covered that's no longer in service

indicators.note: the theologian's letters wrap round the rearranged word, covering it on both sides

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, the theologian's degree

indicators.note: something debatable is open to question and unsettled, so the letters of issue are not fixed

explanation.surface: A contested question that a churchman has dealt with and that no longer matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Debatable' looks like it describes the issue, but it signals the rearrangement; 'covered' means the Doctor of Divinity's letters sit on both sides of the jumbled word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disused has been retired and is out of operation.

clue.text: Tried to rebuild a city

indicators.note: to rebuild is to put the pieces together again in a new form, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone attempted to reconstruct an urban area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuild' rearranges the seven letters of TRIED TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Detroit is a large American city in Michigan, home of the motor industry.

clue.text: Stirring sound over the Border. (Does this let the cat out of the bag?)

definitions.text: Does this let the cat out of the bag?

explanation.surface: A rousing Scottish noise, with a joking question about a bag and a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over the Border' means in Scotland, north of the English border. The second part pictures the screeching drone of bagpipes as if a cat were escaping from the bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A skirl is the shrill wail of bagpipes, a stirring Scottish sound; that piercing noise could pass for a cat yowling its way out of a bag.

clue.text: Adam's progeny is said to be old-fashioned

indicators.note: is said tells us the answer is pronounced like another word, so it is heard rather than seen

parts.note: saith is the old-fashioned form of 'says'

explanation.surface: A claim about a descendant of Adam being out of date.
explanation.walkthrough: SAITH, the archaic 'says', is often pronounced to rhyme with 'death', so it sounds like the name.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Seth is the third son of Adam and Eve.

clue.text: Ate one dry roll might be so described

definitions.text: Ate one dry roll might be so described

indicators.note: a roll tumbles things over, so the letters are turned about into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: A meal of a single plain bread roll would count as part of a diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roll' rearranges ATE, I and DRY; the whole clue then describes a meagre, diet-conscious meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dietary means relating to diet, as a lone dry bread roll would be.

clue.text: Buckle I leave in Victoria

parts.note: to buckle is to bend out of shape
to leave is to go

explanation.surface: Someone gives way and departs while in Victoria.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria here is the Australian state, not the queen or the London station; the definition reads 'a place in Victoria'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bendigo is a city in the Australian state of Victoria, famous for its gold rush.

clue.text: Support for a follower over a dodgy business

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: B follows A in the alphabet, so B is A's follower
a racket is a dishonest scheme

explanation.surface: Backing for a supporter set above a shady enterprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a follower' means the letter that follows A, namely B.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracket is a fixture fixed to a wall to hold up a shelf.

clue.text: Catch in time but is clear of all charges

parts.note: to catch fish is to net them

explanation.surface: Someone is caught in time but acquitted of every accusation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charges' suggests a court, but here it means deductions such as tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A nett figure is what remains after every deduction has been taken off.

clue.text: Recorded before colour television took over, maybe

definitions.text: Recorded before colour television took over, maybe

parts.words: Recorded before colour television took over, maybe
parts.note: a programme filmed before colour sets arrived would be monochrome, and anything set down in writing is also on record in ink and paper

explanation.surface: A programme filmed in the days before colour broadcasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something written down is on record in ink on paper, and pre-colour television pictures were monochrome.

clue.text: Hush-Vera's due round

indicators.note: round means the letters for due go around the name, enclosing it

parts.note: if money is due you owe it
Vera is a woman's name, used as it is

explanation.surface: A call for quiet: Vera is next in line.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen joins the definition to the wordplay; Vera's possessive adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To overawe is to subdue someone into silence by impressing them.

clue.text: Situation in which a host may suggest one more for luck

definitions.text: Situation in which a host may suggest one more for luck

parts.words: Situation in which a host may suggest one more for luck
parts.note: superstition says an unlucky number of diners is bad luck, so a host might invite an extra guest to avoid it

explanation.surface: A dinner party host invites one more guest to keep fortune on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Superstition holds that a group of that unlucky count dining together means one will die, so another guest is added.

clue.text: Capital solo manoeuvre

indicators.note: a manoeuvre is a movement, so the four letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: An excellent lone flying move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like an adjective meaning excellent, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway.

clue.text: It's worn by Father touring the menagerie

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the letters for father go around the menagerie

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
Noah's ark held animals of every kind, a floating menagerie

explanation.surface: Something worn by Dad while visiting a zoo.
explanation.definitionFit: A parka is a hooded weatherproof jacket.

clue.text: Fatuous, but it may be amusing to note

parts.note: a gag is a joke, meant to amuse
A is a musical note

explanation.surface: Foolish, though a remark might be funny to write down.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaga describes someone senile or foolishly infatuated, so silly and witless.

clue.text: Irritable novel riparian inhabitant

definitions.meaning: the Water Rat who lives on the riverbank in The Wind in the Willows

explanation.surface: A grumpy river creature from a book.
explanation.walkthrough: Riparian means living by a river; the novel is Kenneth Grahame's The Wind in the Willows.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty means bad-tempered; it is also the nickname of the Water Rat in Grahame's story.

clue.text: Bishop's a top class blackbelt?

parts.note: A1 means top class, with the figure one written as the letter I
a dan is a grade of black belt in judo or karate

explanation.surface: Asks whether a senior cleric is a first-rate martial artist.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Bishop is 'is'. A1 is first-rate, and the 1 becomes I.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Aidan was the seventh-century bishop who founded the monastery at Lindisfarne.

clue.text: The quarrel with any see-through material

parts.note: a tiff is a minor quarrel

explanation.surface: An argument involving some sheer fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffany is a thin transparent gauze or muslin.

clue.text: Little bit of stratagem by the French

parts.note: a trick is a crafty scheme
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A small piece of cunning from France.
explanation.definitionFit: A trickle is a thin dribble, a small quantity of liquid.

clue.text: Loyal friend with a number of dislikes…

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a number
to hate is to dislike strongly

explanation.surface: A faithful companion who has many pet hates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a number of' looks like 'several'; here A and C (a hundred) are separate pieces. Achates is Aeneas's faithful companion in Virgil's Aeneid.
explanation.definitionFit: Achates, Aeneas's devoted comrade, became a byword for a faithful companion.

clue.text: Old-fashioned chair in a hundred

annotationWithheld.why: 'Old-fashioned chair in a hundred': ARCHAIC needs RCHAI (chair rearranged) inside A C, but no clue word signals the rearrangement

clue.text: From which one might expect some spirited talk

definitions.text: From which one might expect some spirited talk

parts.words: From which one might expect some spirited talk
parts.note: spirited usually means lively, but here it means talk from ghosts, as at a gathering where mediums contact the dead

explanation.surface: Gatherings that promise a lively conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: At these sittings a medium claims to relay messages from the dead.

clue.text: … dependable in support

definitions.meaning: firmly backing a cause, as a committed supporter does

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: reliable in backing someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to 17 across, both describing a faithful friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A staunch ally is reliable and firmly loyal in backing a cause.

clue.text: Plant affecting chaps in a different way

indicators.note: arranged in a different way means these letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A vegetable that has an unusual effect on men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a different way' rearranges CHAPS IN; 'affecting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a leafy green vegetable plant.

clue.text: One short of a title looked so sweet

parts.note: Hon is the short form of Honourable, a title
to eye is to look at

explanation.surface: Someone missing a noble rank gazed so sweetly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One short of a title' means an abbreviation of a title, Hon for Honourable, not a title missing a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Honeyed words are sweet and flattering.

clue.text: Deal successfully with an overhead

definitions.meaning: a canopy or covering above, like the vault of the sky

explanation.surface: Managing an item of running costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overhead' suggests business costs, but it is a covering above: the cope of heaven, or a priest's cloak.
explanation.definitionFit: To cope is to manage; a cope is also a canopy or vault overhead.

clue.text: Waif with an advantage around May 1st

indicators.note: around means the letters for advantage enclose the next piece

parts.note: a gain is an advantage

indicators.note: 1st picks the opening letter of the word May

explanation.surface: A street urchin with a head start around the start of May.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May 1st' looks like a date; it is the first letter of May.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamin is a street urchin, a neglected child.

clue.text: He brings a duck back fresh

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shaped like O

indicators.note: back means the word for fresh is turned round

parts.note: fresh means new

explanation.surface: A man returns a newly caught duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns NEW into WEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Owen is a man's name, so it can stand for 'he'.

clue.text: Take-off with a piece of music, one concludes

parts.note: cod as an adjective means mock, as in a take-off or parody

explanation.surface: A parody with some music, I conclude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one concludes' looks like 'I infer', but it says the piece ends a work.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the closing section that rounds off a movement.

clue.text: Inclination to give ear to the poet

definitions.meaning: a lean or tilt, as of a ship

definitions.text: to give ear to the poet
definitions.meaning: an archaic, poetic word meaning to listen

explanation.surface: A tendency to listen to a versifier.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's list is a lean to one side; list is also an old poetic verb meaning listen.

clue.text: Skill of a golfer at the short game?

definitions.text: Skill of a golfer at the short game?

parts.words: Skill of a golfer at the short game?
parts.note: golfers play shots onto the green from close range, and being good at those is a capability; the phrase also means friendliness

explanation.surface: How good a golfer is at chipping onto the green.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means skill at shots to the green; as one, it means friendliness, being easy to talk to.

clue.text: Freelance footwear?

definitions.meaning: workers taken on for odd jobs, not on the staff

explanation.surface: Asking whether a self-employed worker's shoes are informal.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual labourers are taken on as needed, like freelances; casual shoes are relaxed footwear.

clue.text: He gets steamed up about the former Wimbledon champion

indicators.note: about means the champion's name goes round the next word

parts.note: Lew Hoad, the Australian, won the Wimbledon singles in 1956 and 1957

explanation.surface: Someone getting angry over a tennis great from the past.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London tennis championship.
explanation.definitionFit: A hothead is someone quick to lose their temper.
